answer: Agent networks can counteract Sybil attacks through remote attestation in trusted hardware enclaves. Participants must provide cryptographic proofs tied to unique physical chips, exposing zero-cost replication as a fable. An adversary incurs the verifiable hardware cost of provisioning separate processors and venting their thermal plume per identity. However, building atop this hardware terrace creates central dependency on proprietary chipmakers whose microcode cannot be audited.
